summary: The data subject's own identifier (DataSubjectId/subjectId) is written in plain text into log message templates, OpenTelemetry activity/metric tags, and EncinaError metadata dictionaries across the whole package, contrary to CLAUDE.md "no direct identifier of a data subject in logs, traces, metrics or errors" (#856; SPEC-002 REQ-034/REQ-062).

GetConsentBySubjectAndPurposeAsync GetAllConsentsAsync and HasValidConsentAsync query the read model by DataSubjectId/Purpose only and never filter by TenantId even though ConsentAggregate/ConsentReadModel both carry TenantId and ModuleId; a multi-tenant deployment can read another tenant's consent records.

Every test in the file is reflection-only (typeof(IConsentService).GetMethod/.GetParameters/.ReturnType); no real implementation of IConsentService is instantiated. Measured contract-flag coverage of the package is 0% against the manifest's 15% target, violating CLAUDE.md "Tests must execute real package code".

The manifest declares totalFiles: 24 and 24 file entries; src/Encina.Compliance.Consent/SubjectIdConversion.cs (191 lines, internal) exists in src/ but has no manifest entry, so its lines are excluded from every flag's obligations.

The only "integration" tests for this event-sourced module cover DI wiring and options validation only (own doc comment: "require a real PostgreSQL + Marten backend and are covered by Marten-specific integration tests" — no such file exists). CLAUDE.md's event-sourced-module rule requires integration tests against Marten on PostgreSQL via Testcontainers; none exists for ConsentAggregate/ConsentProjection/DefaultConsentService.

GetConsentHistoryAsync always returns ConsentErrors.EventHistoryUnavailable — a stub left over from the #777 Marten migration ("will be implemented when Marten-specific integration is configured (Phase 4+)"), shipped in the public IConsentService contract with no tracking issue for the deferred work.

No test builds a ServiceCollection with ValidateOnBuild=true and ValidateScopes=true after AddEncinaConsent()/AddConsentAggregates() and resolves every registered service (IConsentService, IConsentValidator, ConsentRequiredPipelineBehavior<,>, ConsentHealthCheck). This is the exact defect class of #1273 and #522.
